ety.text: Of unknown origin. Possibly of North Germanic origin.

ex: Some tardy cripple bore the countermand, / That came too lag to see him buried.
the lag end of my life

senses.d: Last made; hence, made of refuse; inferior.
ex: We know your thoughts of us, that laymen are lag souls, and rubbish of remaining clay.

senses.d: A gap, a delay; an interval created by something not keeping up; a latency.

ex: Whatever the symptom, lag is a drag. But what causes it? One cause is delays in getting the data from your PC to the game server.
When the lag is low, 2 or 3 seconds perhaps, Internet chatters seem reasonably content.

senses.d: One sentenced to transportation for a crime.

A method of deciding which player is to start. Both players simultaneously strike a cue ball from the baulk line to hit the top cushion and rebound down the table; the player whose ball finishes closest to the baulk cushion wins.
One who lags; that which comes in last.
ex: the lag of all the flock

senses.d: The fag-end; the rump; hence, the lowest class.

A stave of a cask, drum, etc.; especially (engineering) one of the narrow boards or staves forming the covering of a cylindrical object, such as a boiler, or the cylinder of a carding machine or steam engine.
To fail to keep up (the pace), to fall behind.
ex: Lazy beast! / Why last art thou now? Thou hast never used / To lag thus hindmost
Brown skeletons of leaves that lag / My forest-brook along

senses.d: To cover (for example, pipes) with felt strips or similar material.
ex: Spun glass mattresses are used for lagging the boiler, which has three Ross pop safety valves on the front ring.
Outside seems old enough: / Red brick, lagged pipes, and someone walking by it / Out to the car park, free.
My phone is starting to lag.

senses.d: To transport as a punishment for crime.
ex: She lags us if we poach.
If a fellow gave them trouble being lagged they let him have it hot and heavy in the bridewell.
Interest in the scandal will never lag.
The weight would lagge thee that art wont to flye.

es:retrasar.gl: to delay, to set back, to slow down, to postpone, to retard, to hold up, to put back
